item.title: Yle poll: SDP support at 25%, Centre overtakes Finns Party
item.description: The Social Democratic Party has strengthened its position as Finland’s most popular party, according to a new opinion poll published by Yle, even as the party faced weeks of public scrutiny over allegations of inappropriate behaviour. Support for the SDP rose to 25.0 per cent in the latest survey, an increase of 1.1 percentage points from the previous measurement. The gap to the second-placed National Coalition Party has grown to more than six percentage points.

item.title: Two Finnish tourists killed in avalanche in northern Italy
item.description: Two Finnish tourists have died in an avalanche in northern Italy after being caught while skiing outside marked slopes, according to Italian public broadcaster Rai. The avalanche occurred on Thursday afternoon in the Alps in the South Tyrol region, near the village of Solda. Italian authorities received the first alert shortly before 1.30 pm local time. Rai reported that the victims were Finnish nationals engaged in freeriding on an off-piste slope when the avalanche struck.

item.title: Russian general Vladimir Alekseyev shot in Moscow
item.description: A senior Russian military intelligence official was shot several times in Moscow on Friday and taken to hospital, Russian authorities said. Lieutenant General Vladimir Alekseyev, deputy director of Russia’s military intelligence agency GRU, was attacked in the stairwell of his apartment building in north-west Moscow. The gunman fled the scene. Russia’s Investigative Committee said an unknown person fired several shots at Alekseyev inside a residential building.

item.title: Media: Sauli Niinistö considered for EU Russia envoy role
item.description: Former Finnish president Sauli Niinistö is being considered for a new European Union special envoy role tasked with reopening dialogue with Russian president Vladimir Putin, according to the Italian newspaper La Repubblica. The paper reported that the idea was discussed on Thursday in Paris during talks between French president Emmanuel Macron, European Commission president Ursula von der Leyen, and European Council president António Costa.

item.title: State data breach exposes details of up to 50,000 officials
item.description: A large data breach at Finland’s state information and communications technology provider has exposed work-related details of up to 50,000 government employees, including staff across all ministries. The breach targeted a mobile device management system operated by the State Centre for ICT Services, known as Valtori. The incident was detected on 30 January and disclosed publicly last week as investigations expanded the estimated scope.

item.title: Finland at the Olympics: Kärävä into slopestyle final, Lehto 15th
item.description: Finland opened its second full day of competition at the Milan–Cortina Winter Olympics with mixed results as Anni Kärävä secured a place in the women’s freeski slopestyle final and Elian Lehto fell short of expectations in the men’s downhill. Kärävä advanced to Monday’s final after qualifying inside the top 12 despite a fall on her second run. Lehto placed 15th in Bormio, more than two seconds behind the winner, after a run that failed to match his early-season form.

item.title: Orpo confirms willingness to continue as National Coalition leader
item.description: Prime Minister Petteri Orpo said on Saturday that he is ready to continue as leader of Finland’s National Coalition Party as it prepares for its summer party congress, where his tenure will reach nearly ten years. Orpo made the announcement during the party’s leadership days in Helsinki, where he delivered a policy address focused on the economy, public finances, and security. item.title: Major fire destroys Jokioinen Leipä bread factory
item.description: A fire destroyed the main bakery of Jokioinen Leipä bread factory in the municipality of Jokioinen in southern Finland early on Sunday morning. The blaze broke out shortly after 4.30am at the company’s factory on Leivänkuja. Flames spread through the structure and reached the roof. Rescue services fought the fire through the morning. Authorities said the building will be lost. The bakery stood empty at the time of the fire. No injuries were reported.

item.title: Snowfall and shifting temperatures ahead after prolonged cold
item.description: A prolonged spell of cold and dry winter weather across Finland is set to give way to more variable conditions during the week beginning 9 February, according to meteorologists from Foreca and the Finnish Meteorological Institute. High pressure that has dominated the country for weeks is moving south. In its wake, cloud cover and snowfall increase across large parts of Finland. Night-time temperatures remain low, while daytime conditions turn more unsettled.

item.title: Lindsey Vonn undergoes surgery after Olympic downhill fall
item.description: Lindsey Vonn underwent surgery on a fractured left leg after a heavy crash during the women’s downhill final at the Milan–Cortina Winter Olympics on Sunday, with doctors confirming her condition is stable. The 41-year-old American skier fell just 13 seconds into her run on the Olimpia delle Tofane course in Cortina d’Ampezzo.
